transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well, hi Dr. Smith. I, uh, I came in because... well, people have been pointing out how I'm acting lately. Like, they can actually see me moving like I’m underwater, you know? Taking forever to just answer a simple question or even get out of a chair. It's like gravity got turned up. Or, on the flip side, I'll be pacing my apartment, just walking back and forth, rubbing my hands together like I’m trying to shake off a really bad customer service call. Which, by the way, happens all the time at work. Just yesterday, this lady yelled at me for twenty minutes about a refund policy I didn't even write. I mean, I just answer the phones, I don't make the rules. She kept saying she was going to get me fired, and I was just sitting there thinking about how the headset always pinches my left ear. It's a cheap plastic one, not like the ones they use in the commercials. Anyway, yeah, that's kind of why I'm here. The moving slow and the pacing thing.
Have you ever had periods lasting several days where you felt unusually energetic, didn't need much sleep, or felt like your thoughts were moving so fast you couldn't keep up with them?

No, I don't... I don't think I've ever felt like that. Like, too much energy? No, definitely not. If anything, I'm always just trying to scrape together enough energy to get through my shift. I mean, speaking of sleep, I tried this new chamomile tea the other night because my neighbor swore by it. She's this older lady, always gardening. She has these huge tomato plants that completely take over her side of the fence. Anyway, she gave me a box of this tea, said it would knock me right out. But honestly, it just tasted like hot grass. And then I was up half the night anyway, just listening to the pipes in my building clank. They do that around 3 AM, every single night. It sounds like someone hitting a wrench against a radiator. I told the landlord, but he just ignores my texts. He's probably too busy fixing up the empty units so he can charge more rent. But yeah, no, I don't get those super energetic days you're talking about. Just... normal tired, mostly.
Have you noticed any changes in your memory, your ability to focus, or any new physical health problems lately?

Memory? No, I don't think so. My memory is fine, and I haven't had any new physical problems like catching a cold or anything. I mean, focusing at work is always a little annoying, but that's mostly because they just updated our ticketing software. It’s supposed to be this huge upgrade, but the text is incredibly small now and all the buttons are gray. 

The guy who did the mandatory training video for it had this really deep, monotone voice. It sounded exactly like the narrator from those old nature documentaries about insects. I used to watch those all the time when I was in middle school. We had them on VHS, and my brother and I would always fight over who got to use the tape rewinder. We had one of those rewinders that was shaped like a red sports car, you know the ones? The headlights would actually light up when it was spinning the tape back. It was pretty loud, honestly, it would just whir on the carpet... but, uh, wait. What were we talking about? 

Oh, right, my focus and health. Yeah, no, no real changes there. Just the usual.

How long have you been experiencing these feelings of being 'underwater' or feeling restless and pacing, and have there been any periods of a few months or longer where you felt completely like your normal self?

Well, let's see... it's been a while now. I'd say about two years and maybe three months? Yeah, it started right after I got fired from my old customer support job. Which was completely unfair, by the way. They let me go because they said my call times were too long, but they never factored in that I was the one getting all the complicated technical issues. Everyone else was just doing password resets. Passwords are so annoying now, aren't they? You need a capital letter, a number, a special character, and the blood of a unicorn just to log into your electricity bill. I had this one password that was just a quote from a movie, but then they made me change it, and I kept forgetting the new one. I ended up having to write it on a sticky note under my keyboard, which is exactly what IT tells you not to do. They sent out this whole memo about security best practices, and it had clip art of a burglar in a striped shirt. Who even wears striped shirts to rob a place anymore? It's like something out of an old cartoon. But, uh... yeah, so it's been about two years and three months since all this started, and no, I haven't really had any breaks where I felt totally normal again. It's just been pretty constant since they let me go.
